SMTO-GWT-0009 — This Gateway is already linked to an SMTO

GUID: 60d178e2-76e9-4cd7-a795-05e8e177fb59
Slug: gateway-already-paired
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • Each Gateway trusts only one SMTO. This one already trusts an SMTO with a different identity (another SMTO, or this one before a reinstall), so it refused this link and changed nothing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages that computer which SMTO the Gateway is meant to work with. If another SMTO already uses it, linking this one would cut that SMTO off.
  2. If this SMTO should take over (for example, you reinstalled SMTO), ask them to stop the Gateway, run its pairing reset command on that computer, and start it again. Only a reset on that computer frees the Gateway to trust a new SMTO.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on that Gateway's row. SMTO links automatically to a Gateway that has been reset.
  4. Before re-running earlier tasks, check whether their work on that computer already finished. A lost connection doesn't prove that earlier work didn't run.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway's row shows Connected and tasks run on it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't reset the pairing if another SMTO still depends on this Gateway.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A pairing challenge or pairing request was refused because the Gateway's saved pairing state is already paired with a controller.

What this means

  • Pairing admission or challenge creation found that the Gateway's persisted state was already paired, including a state change before a challenge was committed. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Pairing admission or challenge creation found that the Gateway's persisted state was already paired, including a state change before a challenge was committed.

How to diagnose it

  • Check which controller owns the existing pairing and whether this attempt reused a stale challenge.

How to fix it

  • The Gateway's client-auth/pairing.json (under GATEWAY_TLS_STATE_DIR) is already paired, so /pair/challenge or /pair returned gateway_already_paired. Confirm which controller owns it; if this Server should replace it, stop the Gateway and run its reset command (for example ./smto-gateway-linux-x86_64 reset, ./src/gateway_agent/reset.sh or python -m gateway_core.reset) as the same OS account and state directory, then reconnect.
  • Use the existing pairing or deliberately reset it through the supported local Gateway pairing flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing controller authenticates, or a deliberate local reset establishes the intended new pairing.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
